html:
The Natchez were a people of the lower Mississippi, around what is now Natchez, Mississippi. They kept up the ways of the Mississippian mound builders into the 1700s, longer than almost anyone, which makes French accounts of them a window on that world.

They were ruled by a chief called the Great Sun, who lived on a mound beside a temple where a sacred fire was kept burning. Society was ranked into Suns, Nobles, Honoured People and commoners, and by custom the higher ranks married commoners. When a Great Sun died, wives and servants were sometimes killed to go with him. Their main ceremonial centre is now known as the Grand Village of the Natchez.

The French built Fort Rosalie on their land in 1716. In 1729, after a French commander demanded the site of one of their villages, the Natchez attacked the fort and killed most of the settlers, in the Natchez revolt. French and Choctaw forces struck back; many Natchez were killed or sold into slavery in the Caribbean. Survivors took refuge with the Chickasaw, Creek and Cherokee. Their neighbours included the Tunica and Houma.
